gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-hanunoo: Gugi draws every stroke, vertical or horizontal, at the same weight, with tall lowercase nearly touching the capitals. Noto Sans Hanunoo sits beneath it as a plain sans, its lowercase filling the height and its open terminals easing the heading's bluntness.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-hebrew: Bold and distinctive, Gugi holds its line width constant from start to finish, with open-cut terminals. And Noto Sans Hebrew meets it with a modern, professional ease, its curves leaving wide gaps before they reach the stems.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-hk:
Gugi comes first, with crossbars as thick as its stems.

Noto Sans HK follows as a clean sans with large lowercase forms and brush ends lifted away before each curve closes, so a long stretch of text keeps moving without clogging.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-imperial-aramai: Strokes of constant width, like bent pipe, give Gugi its bold, distinctive look, with tall lowercase nearly reaching the capitals. Noto Sans Imperial Aramaic adds approachable, open-pincer curves.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-inscriptional-p: Gugi's ruler-straight line weight is the first thing you notice, bold and unwavering from stem to curve. Noto Sans Inscriptional Parthian answers it with big open eyes on every e and a, which makes the pair's strongest quality its clean, wide-open contrast.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-jp: Gugi leads with n arches as thick as the stems beside them, plus tall lowercase that nearly meets the capitals. But Noto Sans JP, a plain sans with a very tall x-height, would make the heading feel crowded if it were set small.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-kaithi: Gugi keeps even its thin joins no thinner than the stems, with terminals cut open so the counters flow outward. And Noto Sans Kaithi, a plain sans with an open channel in the e, lets a longer passage glide along with its lowercase filling the line like capitals.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-kannada: Noto Sans Kannada is approachable and contemporary, with s curves that open wide at both ends and a gentle bump up to capitals. And Gugi, cut like ribbon of constant width, makes the pair's strongest quality a friendly, bold contrast.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-kayah-li: Clean and neutral, Noto Sans Kayah Li lifts its brush ends away before the curves close, and its capitals barely rise above the lowercase. Gugi's neon-tube strokes sit above it.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-kharoshthi: Noto Sans Kharoshthi reads approachable and contemporary, its curves never closing back on themselves and its lowercase forming a thick, dark stripe through each line. Gugi then arrives with a blunt, round-tip marker feel from end to end, giving the heading a bold, distinct voice.
